newsitem.title: USA: Disney to take steps for the deaf at its two parks.
newsitem.headline: Disney to take steps for the deaf at its two parks.

text.p: Walt Disney Co has agreed to provide various special services for the deaf and those who have trouble hearing at its two theme parks in the United States, the Justice Department said Friday.

It said the agreement provides for sign language interpreters and captioning systems for the attractions, including more than 100 rides, parades and staged performances at Disneyland in California and Walt Disney World in Florida.

Disney has agreed to regularly provide interpreters at certain attractions, make the schedule available to guests and provide interpreters at specific attractions if requested two weeks in advance, department officials said.

They said Disney also will provide captioning for some attractions and will advertise the availability of interpreters, captioning and listening devices to increase the volume for hard-of-hearing guests.
Before reaching the agreement, Disney already had begun to offer some of the services, they said.
The Justice Department, which enforces a 1990 law barring discrimination against persons with disabilites, contacted Disney after deaf patrons had complained.
